title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — if peccatum figurative here, orthodox arms vs Pelagius fail; tip before GAR Resp.3
pass_a_gloss: Take peccatum here as mere figure (cause named for the effect) and the Orthodox lose this text against Pelagius and Pighius. Take it in the proper sense and you cannot also call it that figure. The two readings cannot both stand.
pass_b_english: If the name of sin is not taken properly in this place, but figuratively, by that figure by which the antecedent is put for the consequent, how do the Orthodox argue from this place against Pelagius and Pighius? And, if it is taken properly, how is it at the same time taken figuratively?
source_text: Si peccati nomen non accipitur proprie hoc loco, sed figurate, ea figura, qua ponitur antecedens pro consequente, quomodo ex hoc loco argumentantur adversus Pelagium & Pighium Orthodoxi? Et, si accipitur proprie, quomodo simul accipitur figurate?

choices.choice: Proper vs figurative peccatum cannot both arm and disarm the Orthodox; tip before GAR Resp.3
